asset_role: visual-only whitewater breakup mask multiplied by solver-authored aeration; no hydraulic, collision, wet-mask, bathymetry, or raft-force authority
generation_method: project-directed generation of an orthographic sparse Colorado River whitewater lace and bubble-cluster mask
prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: tileable grayscale breakup-mask texture for an Unreal Engine solver-driven whitewater material. Primary request: create a seamless square foam-lace breakup mask inspired by the sediment-bearing Colorado River at Hance Rapid in Grand Canyon. Subject: sparse irregular branching off-white whitewater lace, elongated downstream streaks, broken scalloped crests, turbulent holes, and small bubble clusters with large connected black open-water regions; natural downstream direction plus cross-current variation to avoid stripes. Style/medium: physically plausible monochrome data texture, pure black background, white and mid-gray foam filaments, high dynamic range, crisp at major strands with softer fine bubbles. Composition/framing: orthographic top-down data texture only, fills the square, perfectly seamless on all four edges, no single focal feature. Constraints: mask data only; black must dominate at least 70 percent; no water color, no normal-map colors, no riverbank, no rocks, no horizon, no perspective, no baked lighting, no shadows, no text, no logos, no watermark; avoid closed cellular honeycomb cracks, regular sine bands, radial spirals, and obvious tiling seams.

texture.encoding: RGB grayscale breakup mask sampled from the red channel

limitations: The asset is procedural visual infill rather than measured Hance foam imagery or rapid-specific calibration.
Mirrored GPU addressing is required because opposite source-image borders are not byte-identical.
The material must multiply this texture by solver-derived foam and speed channels so it cannot paint whitewater into calm or dry cells.
In-engine visual, guide, water-VFX, and target-hardware acceptance remain required.
